title: Reload a service's configuration without restarting it
summary: Apply changes to a service's configuration file (like a web server config) without stopping and starting the service. This keeps the service running and avoids downtime.
prerequisites: You have edited the service's configuration file.
The service supports reloading (most daemons like nginx, apache, ssh do).

steps.explain: Reload the configuration for a specific system service. Replace <SERVICE> with the name of the service (e.g., nginx, apache2, ssh).

placeholders.name: SERVICE
placeholders.description: The name of the service to reload (e.g., nginx, apache2).

alternatives.explain: Reload a user-level service (like pipewire) instead of a system service.

placeholders.name: SERVICE
placeholders.description: The name of the user service to reload.

warnings: If the service does not support reloading, this command will fail. You may need to restart the service instead.
This does not reload systemd unit files. If you changed a .service file, use 'systemctl daemon-reload' first.

rollback.explain: If the reload causes issues, restart the service to apply the configuration cleanly. Note: The restart command is not on this page, so consult the systemctl restart documentation or use the system's service management GUI.
